content: 1. Continue using metronidazole even if your symptoms improve or disappear. This ensures that future infections are less likely to become resistant to vaginal metronidazole or similar medications. 2. Vaginal metronidazole is an antibiotic commonly prescribed to treat bacterial vaginosis, an infection caused by specific bacteria. However, its effectiveness may vary depending on the bacteria responsible for the infection. 3. In some regions, bacteria may have developed resistance to vaginal metronidazole, reducing its efficacy. Your healthcare provider will determine if this medication is appropriate for your condition. 4. Vaginal metronidazole may also be used for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Additionally, metronidazole is available in topical, oral, and injectable forms for other uses. 5. Vaginal metronidazole works by damaging the DNA of certain bacteria, effectively killing them. 6. Vaginal metronidazole is available as Nuvesse, Vandazole, and generic formulations, typically supplied as a 0.75% vaginal gel for intravaginal use. 7. Store vaginal metronidazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. 8. Common side effects of vaginal metronidazole include headache, vaginal itching, stomach pain, nausea, heavy or painful menstrual periods, sore throat, rash, diarrhea, breast pain (specific to Vandazole), and vaginal yeast infections. Notify your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. 9. Vaginal yeast infections may occur during or after treatment with vaginal metronidazole. This medication does not treat yeast infections. If you experience symptoms such as vaginal discharge, itching, or discomfort, consult your healthcare provider, as you may require antifungal treatment. 10. Serious side effects of vaginal metronidazole, though rare, include severe allergic reactions. Stop using the medication and seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, facial or throat swelling, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, stomach cramps, or joint pain. 11. Nervous system problems, such as seizures, peripheral neuropathy (numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet), confusion, or behavioral changes, have been reported with other forms of metronidazole. Discontinue use and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 12. Do not use vaginal metronidazole if you are allergic to metronidazole, Nuvesse, Vandazole, parabens, nitroimidazole derivatives, or any ingredients in the specific product. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients. 13. Vaginal metronidazole may interact with other medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. 14. Avoid consuming alcohol or foods containing alcohol or propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least one day after stopping Nuvesse or three days after stopping Vandazole. Serious side effects may occur. 15. Use vaginal metronidazole only as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. 16. Keep vaginal metronidazole out of reach of children. Avoid sexual activity and the use of vaginal products such as tampons or douches while using this medication. 17. Vaginal metronidazole is for intravaginal use only. If it comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them with cool water and contact your healthcare provider. 18. Before using vaginal metronidazole, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications or supplements you are taking. This helps determine if the medication is suitable for you. 19. If you have a history of nervous system disorders, such as seizures or peripheral neuropathy, inform your healthcare provider before using vaginal metronidazole. 20. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, discuss this with your healthcare provider. The effects of vaginal metronidazole on pregnancy and the unborn baby are not fully known. 21. Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, consult your healthcare provider. You may need to pump and discard breast milk while using the medication and for two days after completing treatment. 22. If you accidentally use too much vaginal metronidazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. 23. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use double or extra doses. 24. Complete the full course of vaginal metronidazole as prescribed, even if your symptoms improve or disappear. This reduces the risk of future infections becoming resistant to the medication.
